column3: “had greedy desires” renders “craved a craving,” and “again” renders “returned.”
“our appetite is gone” renders “our soul (nefesh) is dried up,” and “nothing at all to look at except this manna” renders “nothing at all; to the manna are our eyes.”
“between two millstones” renders “in the hand-mill,” and “cakes baked with oil” renders “a cake of oil,” a phrase whose meaning is uncertain.
“throughout their families” renders “by its clans,” and “Moses was displeased” renders “in the eyes of Moses it was evil.”
“been so hard on” renders “done evil to.”
“at once” renders an emphatic doubled verb, and “my wretchedness” renders “my evil.”
NASB capitalizes “Spirit” and uses “Him” for the feminine Hebrew noun ruach (also in verse 25); “take of” renders “set aside some of.”
“Oh that someone would give us meat” renders “who will feed us meat,” and “we were well-off” renders “it was good for us.”
“a whole month” renders “a month of days” (also in verse 21).
“to be sufficient for them” renders “and one will find (enough) for them” (twice).
“Is the Lord’s power limited?” renders “Is the hand of the LORD short?”, and “come true for you” renders “happen to you.”
“they did not do it again” renders “they did not add”; the verb can also be read “they did not cease,” so the meaning is uncertain.
NASB capitalizes “Spirit” and puts the note about Eldad and Medad in parentheses.
“Would that” renders “who will give,” and NASB capitalizes “Spirit.”
